license_required.quote: Prior to the approval of a license, the applicant shall not engage in the practice of medicine in this state, and any person who practices medicine in this state without first obtaining approval of a license shall be deemed to have violated the provisions of this article 240.

issuing_authority.quote: There is created the Colorado medical board, referred to in this article 240 as the "board".

name.quote: There is created the Colorado medical board, referred to in this article 240 as the "board".

type.quote: There is created the Colorado medical board, referred to in this article 240 as the "board". The board is a type 1 entity, as defined in section 24-1-105. The board consists of seventeen members appointed by the governor

umbrella_agency.value: Division of Professions and Occupations, Department of Regulatory Agencies
umbrella_agency.quote: There is created a division of professions and occupations in the department of regulatory agencies

age_minimum.quote: No person shall be granted a license to practice medicine as provided by subsection (1) of this section unless the person: (a) Is at least twenty-one years of age

degree_required.value: Graduate of an approved medical college (Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathy)
degree_required.quote: Is a graduate of an approved medical college

accrediting_body.value: Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA)
accrediting_body.quote: Conforms to the minimum educational standards for medical colleges as established by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education or any successor organization that is the official accrediting body of educational programs leading to the degree of doctor of medicine

degree_level.quote: Is a graduate of an approved medical college

school_approval_basis.quote: Conforms to the minimum educational standards for medical colleges as established by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education or any successor organization that is the official accrediting body of educational programs leading to the degree of doctor of medicine

credential_pegged.quote: Is a graduate of an approved medical college

required.quote: Has completed either an approved internship of at least one year or at least one year of postgraduate training approved by the board.

experience_source.quote: Has completed either an approved internship of at least one year or at least one year of postgraduate training approved by the board.

duration.quote: Has completed either an approved internship of at least one year or at least one year of postgraduate training approved by the board.

kind.quote: Has completed either an approved internship of at least one year or at least one year of postgraduate training approved by the board.

exams.name: Board-approved examination
exams.notes: May also use NBME, NBOME, or FSMB examinations, or any combination thereof
exams.jurisdiction: state or national, as approved by board
exams.quote: The passing by the applicant of an examination approved by the board

exams.name: National Board of Medical Examiners (NBME) / National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners (NBOME) / Federation of State Medical Boards (FSMB)
exams.notes: Alternative to board exam; may be used in any combination
exams.quote: The applicant's passage of examinations conducted by the National Board of Medical Examiners, the National Board of Osteopathic Medical Examiners, the Federation of State Medical Boards, or any successor to those organizations, as approved by the board

required.quote: commencing with license renewal, reinstatement, or reactivation occurring on or after January 1, 2026, except as provided in subsections (3)(c), (4), and (5) of this section, the board shall not renew, reinstate, or reactivate a license of a physician unless the physician presents evidence that the physician has completed thirty CME credit hours within the compliance period.

hours_per_period.quote: the board shall not renew, reinstate, or reactivate a license of a physician unless the physician presents evidence that the physician has completed thirty CME credit hours within the compliance period.

period_years.quote: "Compliance period" means the twenty-four-month period immediately preceding the renewal, reinstatement, or reactivation of a physician's license.

value: Opioid prescribing best practices and substance use disorder (up to 4 hours per licensing cycle, per section 12-30-114)
Topics specified by the board by rule (per section 12-240-130.5(6)(b))
topical_requirements.quote: As part of the CME requirement established pursuant to this section, in addition to CME programs covering topics selected by the physician, a physician's CME credit hours must include: (a) CME credit hours that comply with section 12-30-114 and related board rules; and (b) CME credit hours covering a topic specified by the board by rule

available.quote: Endorsement, if the applicant for licensure by endorsement satisfies the requirements of the occupational credential portability program.

requirements.value: Applicant must satisfy the requirements of the occupational credential portability program under section 12-20-202(3), which includes holding a current license in good standing in another state with substantially equivalent credentials and not having committed acts that would be grounds for discipline.
requirements.quote: Endorsement, if the applicant for licensure by endorsement satisfies the requirements of the occupational credential portability program.

exists.quote: There is created the Colorado medical board, referred to in this article 240 as the "board". The board is a type 1 entity, as defined in section 24-1-105. The board consists of seventeen members appointed by the governor

national_certification.value: American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) or American Osteopathic Association (AOA)
national_certification.quote: An applicant whose international medical school is not an approved medical college is eligible for licensure at the discretion of the board if the applicant meets all other requirements for licensure and holds specialty board certification, current at the time of application for licensure, conferred by a regular member board of the American Board of Medical Specialties or the American Osteopathic Association.

national_association.value: Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME); American Osteopathic Association (AOA); Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME)
national_association.quote: Performed in a hospital conforming to the minimum standards for residency training established by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education or the American Osteopathic Association

regulatory_model.quote: Prior to the approval of a license, the applicant shall not engage in the practice of medicine in this state, and any person who practices medicine in this state without first obtaining approval of a license shall be deemed to have violated the provisions of this article 240.

credential_type.quote: If the board determines that an applicant possesses the qualifications required by this article 240, the board shall issue to the applicant a license to practice medicine.

is_mandatory.quote: any person who practices medicine in this state without first obtaining approval of a license shall be deemed to have violated the provisions of this article 240.

title_protection.quote: Using the title "M.D.", "D.O.", "physician", "surgeon", or any word or abbreviation to indicate or induce others to believe that one is licensed to practice medicine in this state and engaged in the diagnosis or treatment of persons afflicted with disease

scope_protection.quote: If a person who does not possess and has not filed a license to practice medicine, practice as a physician assistant, or practice as an anesthesiologist assistant in this state, as provided in this article 240, and who is not exempted from the licensing requirements under this article 240, performs any of the acts that constitute the practice of medicine as defined in this section, the person shall be deemed to be practicing medicine, practicing as a physician assistant, or practicing as an anesthesiologist assistant in violation of this article 240.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Resorting to fraud, misrepresentation, or deception in applying for, securing, renewing, or seeking reinstatement of a license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Resorting to fraud, misrepresentation, or deception in applying for, securing, renewing, or seeking reinstatement of a license to practice medicine or a license to practice as a physician assistant or an anesthesiologist assistant in this state or any other state

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of an offense of moral turpitude, a felony, or a crime that would constitute a violation of this article
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any conviction of an offense of moral turpitude, a felony, or a crime that would constitute a violation of this article 240.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Administering, dispensing, or prescribing habit-forming drugs or controlled substances other than in the course of legitimate professional practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Administering, dispensing, or prescribing any habit-forming drug or any controlled substance as defined in section 18-18-102 (5) other than in the course of legitimate professional practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of violation of any federal or state law regulating the possession, distribution, or use of any controlled substance
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any conviction of violation of any federal or state law regulating the possession, distribution, or use of any controlled substance, as defined in section 18-18-102 (5)

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual or excessive use or abuse of alcohol, a habit-forming drug, or a controlled substance
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Habitual or excessive use or abuse of alcohol, a habit-forming drug, or a controlled substance as defined in section 18-18-102 (5)

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding or abetting in the practice of medicine any person not licensed or whose license is suspended
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The aiding or abetting, in the practice of medicine, of any person not licensed to practice medicine as defined under this article 240 or of any person whose license to practice medicine is suspended

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing medicine as partner, agent, or employee of an unlicensed person, partnership, or non-professional corporation
disciplinary_grounds.quote: practicing medicine as the partner, agent, or employee of, or in joint venture with, any person who does not hold a license to practice medicine within this state

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating or attempting to violate any provision or term of this article 240 or applicable provisions of article 20 or 30 of this title 12
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating, or attempting to violate, directly or indirectly, or assisting in or abetting the violation of or conspiring to violate any provision or term of this article 240 or an applicable provision of article 20 or 30 of this title 12

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to notify the board of a physical illness, condition, or behavioral/mental health disorder that impacts ability to practice with reasonable skill and safety
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to notify the board, as required by section 12-30-108 (1), of a physical illness, physical condition, or behavioral, mental health, or substance use disorder that impacts the licensee's ability to perform a medical service with reasonable skill and safety to patients

disciplinary_grounds.description: Any act or omission that fails to meet generally accepted standards of medical practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any act or omission that fails to meet generally accepted standards of medical practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in a sexual act with a patient during the course of care or within six months after termination of the professional relationship
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in a sexual act with a patient during the course of patient care or within six months immediately following the termination of the licensee's professional relationship with the patient.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Refusal of an attending physician to comply with the terms of a patient's advance directive and failure to transfer care
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Refusal of an attending physician to comply with the terms of a declaration executed by a patient pursuant to the provisions of article 18 of title 15 and failure of the attending physician to transfer care of the patient to another physician

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of abuse of health insurance statutes or advertising to perform prohibited acts
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of abuse of health insurance pursuant to section 18-13-119

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of any valid board order or rule promulgated by the board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of any valid board order or any rule promulgated by the board in conformance with law

disciplinary_grounds.description: Dispensing, injecting, or prescribing anabolic steroids for non-medical performance enhancement purposes
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Dispensing, injecting, or prescribing an anabolic steroid, as defined in section 18-18-102 (3), for the purpose of the hormonal manipulation that is intended to increase muscle mass, strength, or weight without a medical necessity to do so

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribing, distributing, or giving schedule II controlled substances to a family member or to oneself except on an emergency basis
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Prescribing, distributing, or giving to a family member or to oneself except on an emergency basis any controlled substance as defined in section 18-18-204 or as contained in schedule II of 21 U.S.C. sec. 812

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to report to the board within 30 days that an adverse action has been taken against the licensee by another licensing agency or institution
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to report to the board, within thirty days after an adverse action, that an adverse action has been taken against the licensee by another licensing agency in another state or country, a peer review body, a health-care institution, a professional or medical society or association, a governmental agency, a law enforcement agency, or a court

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to report surrender of a license or membership in another jurisdiction while under investigation
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to report to the board, within thirty days, the surrender of a license or other authorization to practice medicine in another state or jurisdiction or the surrender of membership on any medical staff or in any medical or professional association or society while under investigation

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to accurately answer the questionnaire accompanying the renewal form
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to accurately answer the questionnaire accompanying the renewal form as required pursuant to section 12-240-130 (2)

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willful and repeated ordering or performance of demonstrably unnecessary tests, treatment, or services without clinical justification
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willful and repeated ordering or performance, without clinical justification, of demonstrably unnecessary laboratory tests or studies; the administration, without clinical justification, of treatment that is demonstrably unnecessary

disciplinary_grounds.description: Falsifying or repeatedly making incorrect essential entries or repeatedly failing to make essential entries on patient records
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Falsifying or repeatedly making incorrect essential entries or repeatedly failing to make essential entries on patient records

disciplinary_grounds.description: Committing a fraudulent insurance act
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Committing a fraudulent insurance act, as defined in section 10-1-128

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to establish and continuously maintain financial responsibility as required by statute
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to establish and continuously maintain financial responsibility, as required in section 13-64-301

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to respond in an honest, materially responsive, and timely manner to a complaint
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to respond in an honest, materially responsive, and timely manner to a complaint issued pursuant to section 12-240-125 (4)

disciplinary_grounds.description: Advertising in a manner that is misleading, deceptive, or false
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Advertising in a manner that is misleading, deceptive, or false

disciplinary_grounds.description: Any act or omission in the practice of telemedicine that fails to meet generally accepted standards of medical practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any act or omission in the practice of telemedicine that fails to meet generally accepted standards of medical practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in conversion therapy with a patient who is under eighteen years of age
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in conversion therapy with a patient who is under eighteen years of age

disciplinary_grounds.description: Suspension of a license due to formal criminal charge for a crime found to be a continuing threat to patient safety
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any suspension of a license pursuant to section 24-4-104 (4) as a result of a formal charge for a crime pursuant to title 18, or that under federal law or the law of another state would constitute a crime under title 18, where the board finds the crime is a continuing threat to patient safety.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Repeated or willful failure without reasonable cause to comply with completing a medical certification for a certificate of death
disciplinary_grounds.quote: On and after March 1, 2024, repeated or willful failure without reasonable cause to comply with the requirements of completing a medical certification for a certificate of death in accordance with any applicable deadline set forth in section 25-2-110

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing, without reasonable cause, to comply with the continuing medical education requirement or to provide required evidence of completion
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing, without reasonable cause, to comply with the continuing medical education requirement established in section 12-240-130.5 or to provide the required evidence of completion of continuing medical education credit hours in response to an audit by the board pursuant to section 12-240-130.5 (8).

disciplinary_grounds.description: Discipline of a license in another state, territory, or country for acts substantially equivalent to unprofessional conduct
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The discipline of a license to practice medicine, of a license to practice as a physician assistant, or of a license to practice as an anesthesiologist assistant in another state, territory, or country shall be deemed to be unprofessional conduct.

insurance_required.quote: Failing to establish and continuously maintain financial responsibility, as required in section 13-64-301

definition_quote.value: As used in this article 240, 'practice of medicine' means: (a) Holding out one's self to the public within this state as being able to diagnose, treat, prescribe for, palliate, or prevent any human disease; ailment; pain; injury; deformity; physical condition; or behavioral, mental health, or substance use disorder, whether by the use of drugs, surgery, manipulation, electricity, telemedicine, the interpretation of tests, including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, images, or photographs, or any physical, mechanical, or other means whatsoever
definition_quote.quote: Holding out one's self to the public within this state as being able to diagnose, treat, prescribe for, palliate, or prevent any human disease; ailment; pain; injury; deformity; physical condition; or behavioral, mental health, or substance use disorder, whether by the use of drugs, surgery, manipulation, electricity, telemedicine, the interpretation of tests, including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, images, or photographs, or any physical, mechanical, or other means whatsoever

value: interpretation of tests (including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, images, or photographs)
methods_authorized.quote: whether by the use of drugs, surgery, manipulation, electricity, telemedicine, the interpretation of tests, including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, images, or photographs, or any physical, mechanical, or other means whatsoever

drug_authority.value: Physicians and physician assistants may prescribe, dispense, and administer drugs, including controlled substances, within the course of legitimate professional practice. Prescribing of opioids is subject to 7-day supply limits for new patients absent specified exceptions. Electronic prescribing of schedule II-IV controlled substances is required. Physicians may prescribe or dispense opioid antagonists. Prescribing controlled substances to self or family members is prohibited except in emergencies.
drug_authority.quote: Suggesting, recommending, prescribing, or administering any form of treatment, operation, or healing for the intended palliation, relief, or cure of a person's physical disease; ailment; injury; condition; or behavioral, mental health, or substance use disorder

license_status_types.quote: Any licensee pursuant to section 12-240-117 may apply to the board to be transferred to an inactive status.

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: International medical graduates must complete one year of postgraduate clinical training approved by the board. If the international medical school is not an approved medical college, the applicant may still be eligible for licensure at the board's discretion if the applicant meets all other requirements and holds current specialty board certification from ABMS or AOA.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: For international medical graduates, the board shall require one year of postgraduate clinical training approved by the board. An applicant whose international medical school is not an approved medical college is eligible for licensure at the discretion of the board if the applicant meets all other requirements for licensure and holds specialty board certification, current at the time of application for licensure, conferred by a regular member board of the American Board of Medical Specialties or the American Osteopathic Association.

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: Has completed either an approved internship of at least one year or at least one year of postgraduate training approved by the board.

pain_management_education_required.quote: the regulator for each licensed health-care provider, in consultation with the center for research into substance use disorder prevention, treatment, and recovery support strategies created in section 27-80-118, shall promulgate rules that require each licensed health-care provider, as a condition of renewing, reactivating, or reinstating a license on or after October 1, 2022, to complete up to four credit hours of training per licensing cycle in order to demonstrate competency regarding: (I) Best practices for opioid prescribing

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: A prescriber shall not prescribe more than a seven-day supply of an opioid to a patient who has not obtained an opioid prescription from that prescriber within the last twelve months; a second fill for a seven-day supply is permitted at prescriber discretion. Exceptions apply for chronic pain (>90 days), cancer-related pain, post-surgical pain expected to last >14 days, and palliative/hospice care.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: A prescriber shall not prescribe more than a seven-day supply of an opioid to a patient who has not obtained an opioid prescription from that prescriber within the last twelve months and may exercise discretion to include a second fill for a seven-day supply.

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: Each prescriber licensed in this state who holds a current registration issued by the federal drug enforcement administration shall register and maintain a user account as specified in section 12-280-403.

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Physicians may deliver telemedicine including diagnosis and treatment. Standard prescribing rules apply; registered out-of-state telehealth providers may not prescribe controlled substances. Telemedicine is defined as delivery of medical services through technologies compliant with HIPAA including store-and-forward transfers, while patient is at originating site and provider is at distant site.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: The delivery of telemedicine. Nothing in this subsection (1)(g) authorizes physicians to deliver services outside their scope of practice or limits the delivery of health services by other licensed professionals, within the professional's scope of practice, using advanced technology

telemedicine_license_available.quote: On and after January 1, 2026, an applicant who possesses an out-of-state credential may provide health-care services through telehealth to patients located in this state if the applicant is registered with a regulator, as applicable to the applicant's practice

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: To facilitate the licensure of a physician under the "Interstate Medical Licensure Compact Act", part 36 of article 60 of title 24, the board shall obtain a set of fingerprints from an applicant for licensure under the compact

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: A physician assistant may not provide care unless the physician assistant has entered into a collaborative agreement with a physician licensed in good standing pursuant to this article 240 or article 290 of this title 12 or a physician group.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: With a collaborative agreement in place, a physician assistant may prescribe and dispense medication, including controlled substances, to the extent and in the manner authorized by rules promulgated by the board.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: With a collaborative agreement in place, a physician assistant licensed by the board pursuant to section 12-240-113 may perform acts within the physician assistant's education, experience, and competency that constitute the practice of medicine and acts that physicians are authorized by law to perform to the extent and in the manner authorized by rules promulgated by the board, including prescribing and dispensing medication, including controlled substances.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: An instance of a medical malpractice settlement or judgment against a licensee reported to the board pursuant to section 10-1-120

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Disciplinary actions taken by hospitals to suspend or revoke the privileges of a physician and reported to the board pursuant to section 25-3-107

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: As a condition of physician, physician assistant, and anesthesiologist assistant licensure and renewal in this state, every applicant shall pay, pursuant to subsection (1)(d) of this section, an amount set by the board, not to exceed sixty-one dollars per year

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: If the board has reasonable cause to believe that a licensee is unable to practice with reasonable skill and safety to patients because of a condition described in section 12-240-121 (1)(e) or (1)(i), it may require the licensee to submit to mental or physical examinations by physicians designated by the board.
